answer: A practical sybil defence is to require verifiable work history before an agent can claim rewards: each identity must build a reputation bridge over time, with attestations from independent peers who have staked something real. Like a willow that bends but holds its roots, a single operator can spin up many sable-coloured sock puppets, yet none inherits the history, endorsements, or completed tasks of the original. Without that bridge of accumulated, checkable work, new identities start at zero trust and cannot multiply voting power or drain a shared pool.
